paper_records.why_added: Foundational mechanics paper on continuum modeling of inter-wire contact friction damping in vibrating cables.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Threatens T1 by proving that inter-wire friction mechanics in slender wire bundles is an established classical discipline.
paper_records.method: Analytical continuum mechanics and boundary value problem formulation
paper_records.material_or_system: Multi-wire stranded cables and parallel wire bundles under tension
paper_records.loading_mode: Transverse flexural vibration under axial tension
paper_records.independent_variables: Inter-wire friction coefficient, normal contact pressure distribution, vibration amplitude
paper_records.dependent_variables: Modal damping ratio, energy dissipation per cycle, flexural wave attenuation
paper_records.model_used: Continuum beam-cable formulation incorporating Coulomb inter-wire friction law
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Micro-slip Coulomb contact model with shear traction boundary conditions
paper_records.experiment_used: Comparison with experimental damping measurements on bridge stay cables
paper_records.experimental_setup: Theoretical formulation validated against laboratory cable vibration test data
paper_records.key_results: Derived analytical expressions for inter-wire slip and frictional damping in cables; proved that energy dissipation is maximized at intermediate slip amplitudes and scales directly with inter-wire contact pressure.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that inter-wire friction in slender wire bundles is fully treatable using continuum mechanics.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not involve shape memory alloys or active pressure control.
directly_verified_statements: Internal friction between adjacent wires produces amplitude-dependent damping and flexural stiffness modulation (Section 2, pp. 2-4).
Contact pressure between wires governs the threshold amplitude required to trigger inter-wire slip (Section 3, pp. 5-7).
inferred_statements: Inter-wire friction mechanics in soft robotic wire bundles follows the same classical contact governing equations.
paper_records.limitations: Linear elastic steel cables only; axial tension required to generate contact pressure.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Demonstrates classical lineage of wire bundle friction mechanics.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Eq. (8)-(14) (inter-wire shear slip equations), Fig. 3 (damping vs vibration amplitude)
paper_records.metadata_conflicts: DOI missing in matrix, verified as ASME Journal of Applied Mechanics 2004.

paper_records.paper_title: Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable
paper_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/A6-2017-Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable.pdf
paper_records.matrix_filename: A6-2017-Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable.pdf
paper_records.why_added: Critical prior art on multi-element cable bending mechanics under external radial contact pressure.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Directly threatens T2 by proving that external radial contact pressure modulating flexural stiffness is prior art.
paper_records.method: Analytical formulation and finite element beam bending simulation
paper_records.material_or_system: Dynamic submarine power cables consisting of multiple metallic conductor cores and polymer fillers
paper_records.loading_mode: Cyclic lateral bending under external radial contact pressure (0.2 MPa)
paper_records.control_variables: Radial contact pressure (0.2 MPa), bending curvature
paper_records.independent_variables: External radial contact pressure, inter-component friction coefficient, bending curvature
paper_records.dependent_variables: Bending moment-curvature relationship, stick-slip threshold, effective flexural rigidity, shear stress distribution
paper_records.model_used: Stick-slip friction beam mechanics with pressure-dependent normal force
paper_records.constitutive_model: Elastic metallic conductor cores and viscoelastic/plastic filler material
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Coulomb friction law with radial contact pressure acting across cylindrical contact interfaces
paper_records.experiment_used: Full-scale dynamic cable bending test rig
paper_records.experimental_setup: Submarine cable clamped under external radial pressure and bent cyclically to evaluate fatigue life
paper_records.key_results: Demonstrated that external radial contact pressure increases the normal force between internal cable components, delaying the onset of slip, increasing initial flexural rigidity, and widening the hysteresis loop.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that external radial confining pressure directly increases inter-element normal force and modulates flexural rigidity under bending.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Applies a constant external radial pressure rather than actively modulating pressure as a variable stiffness control parameter on NiTi.
directly_verified_statements: External radial pressure p directly increases the contact normal force between internal cable elements, delaying the onset of slip to higher curvatures (Section 3, pp. 4-6).
The bending stiffness transitions from a high stick bound to a lower slip bound as inter-element friction is overcome (Section 4, pp. 7-9).
inferred_statements: In soft robotics, modulating chamber pressure p(t) is mechanically identical to varying the radial pressure boundary condition in submarine cables.
paper_records.limitations: Constant radial pressure; copper conductors rather than NiTi superelastic wires.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Direct basis for CONTRA-05: proves active pressure is an experimental boundary condition, closing T2 as mechanics novelty.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Fig. 5 (radial contact pressure schematic), Fig. 8 (moment-curvature curves under radial pressure)
paper_records.metadata_conflicts: DOI missing in matrix, verified as ASME OMAE 2017 paper.
